invariant: CommandCreateClass materializes the declared child before processing inheritance clauses. manageExtends then visits extends before implements and creates only missing supertype quarks. A missing implements target is an interface; a missing extends target is an interface when the child is an interface and otherwise a class. An already materialized target keeps its existing type. This creation sequence also fixes the shared SVEK UID order.
causal_divergence: Rust creates the child first and visits clauses in source order, but parse_supertypes sends every missing target through ensure_entity, whose default is EntityKind::Class. A target first encountered through implements is therefore permanently materialized as a class and consumes a class node identity before a later explicit interface declaration. The resulting glyph, color, element count, and SVEK endpoint IDs differ even though the relationship topology is otherwise correct.
planned_change: Derive the Java supertype kind from the clause mode and the already materialized child's kind, then use ensure_entity_kind so only missing targets receive that kind. Preserve existing target kinds and the child-first, extends-before-implements creation order. Add parser and held-out cases for class implements, interface extends, preexisting conflicting target kinds, multiple comma-separated targets, renamed labels, and reordered later declarations.
